post.description: Stores the user message and a generating assistant message, then generates the answer with the session's provider and model. With Accept: text/event-stream the response is an event stream (see the 200 response); errors found before it starts are ordinary problem details with the statuses below. Otherwise (JSON) the response waits for the answer at most the effective wait (Prefer: wait=N, otherwise the server's default wait, always capped by its maximum; none with Prefer: respond-async): 200 with both messages when it completed, 502 problem details with both messages when it failed, 202 with both messages when it is still being generated. Generation continues unless the server shuts down (the answer then fails as cancelled); the wait only decides the response. 404 session_not_found; 409 session_busy while an earlier answer in the session is still being generated; 422 provider_unavailable or model_not_supported when the session's settings no longer resolve, llm_credential_missing when the provider needs a key and neither X-LLM-Api-Key nor a server key is available; 400 validation_error for a malformed X-LLM-Api-Key (its value is never echoed); 503 server_busy (Retry-After) while the server is shutting down.

parameters.description: text/event-stream for an event stream of the answer; anything else (or none) for JSON
parameters.name: accept

parameters.description: RFC 7240 preferences for the JSON response. wait=N: wait up to N seconds for the answer, capped by the server's maximum (JSON_MAX_WAIT_MS, 195 s unless configured); without it the server's default applies (JSON_DEFAULT_WAIT_MS, 30 s unless configured); respond-async: answer at once without waiting. respond-async wins when both are sent. Unknown or malformed preferences are ignored, never an error.
parameters.name: prefer

parameters.description: Your own API key for this generation's provider. Used for this one generation, then dropped: never stored, logged or returned. Without it the server's own key for the provider is used, if it has one; providers with requiresKey: false need none.
parameters.name: x-llm-api-key

schema.description: Server-sent events, each `event: <name>` plus one `data:` line of JSON: message.created { userMessage, assistantMessage } (the snapshot: content so far), delta { id, attempt, text } (only text after the snapshot), done { assistantMessage } (completed, with usage), error { code, detail, assistantMessage } (failed), message.detached { assistantMessage } (generating where this server cannot follow it; poll the message). A `: ping` comment every 15 s (SSE_PING_INTERVAL_MS). No event ids: a reconnecting client re-attaches and gets a fresh snapshot.

200.description: JSON: the answer completed within the wait. Event stream: the answer as it is generated (generation failures arrive as an error event, the status stays 200)

Preference-Applied.description: The preferences honoured: respond-async, or wait=<seconds waited at most> (the cap when the request asked for more). Absent when none applied. Not a completion guarantee.

get.description: Re-attaches to an assistant message's current attempt, whatever the Accept header: message.created with both messages as they are now (the text so far), then the remaining deltas exactly once and done or error. A message that is already completed or failed gets message.created and done or error; one that is being generated where this server cannot follow it (another process, or a lost generation not yet failed as interrupted) gets message.created and message.detached: poll the message instead. The stream then ends. 404 session_not_found; message_not_found unless it is an assistant message of this session.

schema.description: Server-sent events, each `event: <name>` plus one `data:` line of JSON: message.created { userMessage, assistantMessage } (the snapshot: content so far), delta { id, attempt, text } (only text after the snapshot), done { assistantMessage } (completed, with usage), error { code, detail, assistantMessage } (failed), message.detached { assistantMessage } (generating where this server cannot follow it; poll the message). A `: ping` comment every 15 s (SSE_PING_INTERVAL_MS). No event ids: a reconnecting client re-attaches and gets a fresh snapshot.

200.description: The answer as an event stream
